criteria.name: correctness
criteria.description: Solution is correct for all cases including edge cases (empty string, all-unique, all-same).

criteria.name: optimal_complexity
criteria.description: Achieves O(n) time with a sliding-window / two-pointer approach.  O(n²) brute force scores partial credit.

criteria.name: code_quality
criteria.description: Clean variable names, no dead code, readable structure.

criteria.name: communication
criteria.description: Candidate explained the approach before coding and narrated tradeoffs.

criteria.name: correctness
criteria.description: Blocking semantics are correct: put() blocks when full, get() blocks when empty, no race conditions.

criteria.name: synchronization_strategy
criteria.description: Chooses an appropriate primitive (ReentrantLock + Conditions, synchronized, or Semaphore) and justifies it.

criteria.name: edge_cases
criteria.description: Handles spurious wakeups (while loop, not if), interrupt handling, and capacity=1.

criteria.name: testability
criteria.description: Mentions how to test concurrency: multiple producer/consumer threads, stress test, or deterministic interleaving.

criteria.name: correctness
criteria.description: Standard binary search is correct. First/last position variants correctly handle duplicates and boundaries.

criteria.name: complexity_analysis
criteria.description: States O(log n) time, O(1) space. Explains why the loop invariant guarantees termination.

criteria.name: edge_cases
criteria.description: Handles empty array, single element, target not present, all elements equal to target.

criteria.name: communication
criteria.description: Walked through the invariant (lo ≤ mid < hi) and why mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2 avoids overflow.

criteria.name: correctness_general
criteria.description: General binary tree LCA is correct using recursive post-order traversal. Returns correct node.

criteria.name: bst_optimization
criteria.description: Correctly leverages BST ordering to traverse left/right without full traversal. Explains why this is O(h) vs O(n).

criteria.name: edge_cases
criteria.description: Handles p or q being the root, p being an ancestor of q, nodes not in tree.

criteria.name: communication
criteria.description: Explained the base case and recursive structure clearly before coding.

criteria.name: greedy_analysis
criteria.description: Clearly explains why greedy fails (e.g. coins [1,3,4], target 6: greedy picks 4+1+1 but 3+3 is optimal).

criteria.name: dp_correctness
criteria.description: DP solution is correct. Recurrence dp[i] = min(dp[i - coin] + 1) for each coin is properly implemented.

criteria.name: complexity
criteria.description: States O(amount × coins) time and O(amount) space. Recognises this as unbounded knapsack.

criteria.name: code_quality
criteria.description: Clean implementation with meaningful variable names; handles amount=0 base case.

criteria.name: bfs_correctness
criteria.description: BFS correctly traverses layer by layer; visited set prevents revisiting; all reachable nodes found.

criteria.name: dfs_correctness
criteria.description: DFS cycle detection is correct. For undirected graph, ignores the edge back to the parent.

criteria.name: tradeoff_analysis
criteria.description: Articulates: BFS good for shortest path / layer problems; DFS good for cycle detection / topological sort / backtracking. Stack vs queue.

criteria.name: code_quality
criteria.description: Clean adjacency-list iteration; no off-by-one in the visited check.

criteria.name: correctness
criteria.description: Correctly sorts by start, merges overlapping intervals (end = max(end, interval[1])), produces correct output.

criteria.name: complexity
criteria.description: States O(n log n) for the sort, O(n) for the merge pass. O(n) space for output.

criteria.name: edge_cases
criteria.description: Handles single interval, non-overlapping list, all intervals overlapping into one.

criteria.name: streaming_extension
criteria.description: Suggests a reasonable streaming approach: sorted insert + merge window, or interval tree.

criteria.name: divide_and_conquer
criteria.description: Correctly implements fast exponentiation: pow(x, n//2)² for even n, x * pow(x, n-1) for odd. O(log n) time.

criteria.name: negative_exponent
criteria.description: Handles negative n correctly: pow(x, -n) = 1 / pow(x, n). Handles n = INT_MIN edge case.

criteria.name: overflow_discussion
criteria.description: Discusses integer overflow risks for large n in typed languages; explains Python's arbitrary precision.

criteria.name: communication
criteria.description: Explained the recurrence and why the naive loop is O(n) before presenting the O(log n) solution.

criteria.name: idempotency
criteria.description: Explains idempotency key pattern: client-generated key, deduplication at ingress, exactly-once semantics.

criteria.name: architecture
criteria.description: Clear layered design: API gateway → async queue → processor → datastore.  Reasonable component choices.

criteria.name: consistency
criteria.description: Addresses distributed consistency: outbox pattern or saga, at-least-once + dedup, balance check atomicity.

criteria.name: scalability
criteria.description: Addresses 10k TPS: partitioning strategy, horizontal scaling, back-pressure.

criteria.name: audit_trail
criteria.description: Proposes append-only event log or event sourcing for the audit trail.

criteria.name: algorithm_choice
criteria.description: Compares token bucket vs sliding window log vs fixed window; picks one with justification.

criteria.name: distributed_correctness
criteria.description: Addresses race conditions across servers: Lua script in Redis for atomicity, or accepts slight inaccuracy.

criteria.name: failure_modes
criteria.description: What happens when Redis is down? Fail-open vs fail-closed tradeoff explained.

criteria.name: communication
criteria.description: Structured walk-through: clarifying questions first, requirements, then design.

criteria.name: cap_theorem_accuracy
criteria.description: Correctly states CAP: cannot guarantee C + A + P simultaneously. Explains that P is unavoidable in practice, so choice is C vs A during partition.

criteria.name: consistency_models
criteria.description: Distinguishes eventual consistency, strong consistency (linearizability), and read-your-writes. Gives concrete database examples (Cassandra, Spanner, DynamoDB).

criteria.name: real_world_examples
criteria.description: Cites real systems: Cassandra/DynamoDB as AP, HBase/Spanner as CP. Explains why each chose its trade-off.

criteria.name: communication
criteria.description: Avoided oversimplification; acknowledged PACELC or the nuances of 'partition tolerance'.

criteria.name: fan_out_strategy
criteria.description: Addresses fan-out: push model (write to each recipient queue) vs pull model. Handles celebrities/high-fan-out users.

criteria.name: delivery_guarantees
criteria.description: Explains at-least-once vs exactly-once. Proposes idempotency keys and deduplication for the consumer side.

criteria.name: retry_and_dlq
criteria.description: Designs retry with exponential backoff and dead-letter queue for failed deliveries. Distinguishes transient vs permanent failures.

criteria.name: channel_abstraction
criteria.description: Abstracts over email/SMS/push behind a channel interface so new channels are addable without changing the core dispatcher.

criteria.name: id_generation
criteria.description: Proposes a collision-free ID strategy: base62 encoding of a counter, hash + collision check, or distributed ID service. Discusses length vs collision probability.

criteria.name: redirect_latency
criteria.description: Achieves low-latency redirects: CDN edge caching, in-memory cache (Redis) in front of DB, 301 vs 302 trade-off for browser caching.

criteria.name: storage_estimation
criteria.description: Back-of-envelope: 100M URLs × ~500 bytes ≈ 50 GB — correctly argues this fits in a single DB. Discusses partitioning for write scale.

criteria.name: analytics
criteria.description: Proposes async click counting (Kafka → batch aggregation) rather than synchronous increment to avoid latency on the hot path.

criteria.name: leader_election
criteria.description: Correctly walks through Raft leader election: term increment, RequestVote RPC, majority quorum, split vote resolution.

criteria.name: log_replication
criteria.description: Correctly describes AppendEntries RPC, commit only after majority ACK, follower catching up via log replay.

criteria.name: failure_handling
criteria.description: Explains what happens on leader failure mid-replication: uncommitted entries are safe to replay; committed entries are never lost.

criteria.name: communication
criteria.description: Used concrete term numbers and node counts (e.g. 5-node cluster, quorum = 3) to illustrate.

criteria.name: inverted_index
criteria.description: Correctly describes inverted index: term → posting list (doc_id, term_freq, positions). Explains how Boolean and phrase queries use it.

criteria.name: ranking
criteria.description: Explains TF-IDF or BM25 scoring. Distinguishes recall (find all relevant) from precision (rank them correctly).

criteria.name: real_time_updates
criteria.description: Proposes segment-based indexing (Lucene model): write to in-memory segment, periodically merge/flush. Handles deletes via tombstones.

criteria.name: scale
criteria.description: Addresses 1B docs: index sharding by term hash or doc range, distributed query fan-out and merge.

criteria.name: consistent_hashing
criteria.description: Correctly explains consistent hashing ring: keys map to nodes, adding/removing a node only remaps O(k/n) keys. Virtual nodes for load balance.

criteria.name: replication
criteria.description: Proposes replication factor ≥ 2; explains read/write quorums (R + W > N) for tunable consistency.

criteria.name: eviction_policy
criteria.description: Compares LRU (recency) vs LFU (frequency). Explains approximations (segmented LRU, count-min sketch for LFU) needed at scale.

criteria.name: cold_start
criteria.description: Addresses cache warming: background loader at startup, lazy population, or thundering-herd protection (probabilistic early expiration).

criteria.name: star_structure
criteria.description: Answer follows STAR: clear Situation, specific Task, concrete Actions, measurable Result.

criteria.name: constructive_approach
criteria.description: Shows data-driven or principled pushback — not emotional.  Escalated appropriately if needed.

criteria.name: outcome_and_reflection
criteria.description: States the actual outcome (even if they lost the argument) and what they learned.

criteria.name: conciseness
criteria.description: Stays under ~3 minutes.  No excessive background or tangents.

criteria.name: star_structure
criteria.description: Clear STAR format with a genuinely complex or ambiguous situation.

criteria.name: ownership_evidence

criteria.name: impact

criteria.name: conciseness
criteria.description: Crisp storytelling — sets up the situation quickly, focuses on their actions.

criteria.name: mentoring_approach

criteria.name: outcome

criteria.name: empathy

criteria.name: incident_clarity

criteria.name: personal_role

criteria.name: root_cause_analysis

criteria.name: prevention

criteria.name: prioritization_framework

criteria.name: communication

criteria.name: outcome

criteria.name: reflection

criteria.name: context
criteria.description: Clearly sets the scene: which teams, what the shared goal was, and what made collaboration difficult.

criteria.name: alignment_strategy
criteria.description: Describes concrete steps to build alignment: shared doc/RFC, joint design review, compromise on interface, or escalation path.

criteria.name: outcome
criteria.description: Project shipped or decision was made. States what they learned about cross-team dynamics.

criteria.name: empathy_and_listening
criteria.description: Acknowledges the other team's constraints and perspective, not just their own team's view.

criteria.name: ambiguity_handling
criteria.description: Describes specific techniques: wrote down assumptions, decomposed unknowns, built a prototype to reduce risk, or time-boxed exploration.

criteria.name: ask_vs_proceed

criteria.name: outcome
criteria.description: States whether the approach worked and what they'd adjust if requirements shifted again.

criteria.name: communication
criteria.description: Kept stakeholders informed of assumptions so surprises were minimised.

criteria.name: relevance

criteria.name: learning_process
criteria.description: Describes a structured approach: side project, reading primary sources, pair-programming, or teaching others.

criteria.name: applied_impact
criteria.description: Shows how the new skill changed real work: a design decision, a PR they wouldn't have written before, or a problem they now see differently.

criteria.name: motivation
criteria.description: Explains what drove the learning — curiosity, a painful incident, or a career goal — not just 'it was required'.
